title: Acyclic hypercovers test invertibility of derived sections of the module unit
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes with their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal modules over the pulled-back coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], the actual derived module adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and ordinary derived terminal sections [def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Let $U_\bullet$ and $V_\bullet$ be simplicial objects of $Y_{proet}$ and $X_{proet}$. Assume specified limiting proper-face matching cones [def-sfb-proper-face-matching-arrow] in every degree, with vertex the identity object in degree zero, and singleton matching arrows belonging to the respective pro-etale precoverages. Assume every term is weakly contractible [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. Let $g_n:V_n\to U_n$ be scheme morphisms over $f$, commuting with every simplicial operator. For any internal $\Lambda_Y$-module $M$, assume that for each $n$ the actual ordinary adjunction-unit section map $\Gamma(U_n,M|_{U_n})\to\Gamma(V_n,g_n^*(M|_{U_n}))$, defined by componentLiftSectionPullback of [lem-sfb-component-lift-lisse-section-comparison], is bijective. Then $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ applied to the specified derived module adjunction unit $M[0]\to Rf_*Lf^*M[0]$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category of abelian groups. No lisseness, affineness, w-strict locality, or condition on connected components is assumed.

proof.text: Regard U and V as augmented simplicial objects over the terminal objects of the two small pro-etale sites. Their structure maps supply the augmentations. The given proper-face cones and matching arrows, including the stated terminal object in degree zero, are limiting. Uniqueness of limits identifies any other proper-face matching arrow with the chosen one followed by an isomorphism. Coverings are invariant under this isomorphism, so these are hypercovers in the normalization theorem. The maps g_n and their displayed base and simplicial equations give a natural transformation V to the base change of U.

Apply the canonical exact internal/sectionwise module equivalences to the coefficient module and the inverse/direct-image functors. Their unit and counit compatibility identifies the derived adjunction units as well. For each weakly etale site object U_n or V_n, the site localization equivalence identifies sections of the module at that object with terminal sections of its scheme pullback. The coefficient identifications are the canonical ones induced by pullback from the point. In particular, section restriction along g_n is the displayed componentLiftSectionPullback on U_n, followed by the canonical isomorphism identifying the successive scheme pullbacks with the pullback along V_n to X and then f. No arbitrary isomorphism of section groups is used.

In the alternating-face section complexes, every nonnegative component of the comparison is conjugate to one of the assumed bijective additive section maps. Thus it is invertible as an abelian-group morphism. Negative components are maps between zero objects because the section complexes are extended by zero. For an inverse to the cochain map, take the inverse of each component: multiplying d-prime c = c d by these inverses proves the cochain equation for the inverses. The componentwise inverse identities give inverse complex morphisms. Localization into the ordinary derived category therefore preserves this isomorphism.

Apply acyclic-hypercover pullback normalization to the two hypercovers, their weak contractibility hypotheses, and their simplicial comparison. Its augmentation-normalized comparison isomorphisms identify the localized section-complex map of the previous step with the actual derived-unit section pullback, not just an abstract isomorphism of the two objects. Transport the square back through the exact module equivalences of step 2. The resulting map is derived sections of the specified derived adjunction unit followed by the canonical Leray section comparison and the exact degree-zero pullback comparison. These last factors and the two augmentation comparisons are isomorphisms; cancel them to obtain invertibility of derived sections applied to the unit itself. Only degree-zero coefficients and bounded-below section complexes occur.

theorem componentHypercoverUnitCriterion
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (U : SimplicialObject Y.ProEt) (V : SimplicialObject X.ProEt)
    (g : ∀ n : ℕ, (V _⦋n⦌).left ⟶ (U _⦋n⦌).left)
    (hU : ∃ (C : ∀ n : ℕ, Cone (U.properFaceDiagram n))
        (μ : ∀ n : ℕ, U _⦋n⦌ ⟶ (C n).pt),
      (C 0).pt = Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 Y) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (C n))) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : SimplicialObject.ProperFaceCategory n),
        μ n ≫ (C n).π.app (op b) = U.map b.obj.hom.op) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Presieve.singleton (μ n) ∈ Scheme.ProEt.precoverage Y (C n).pt))
    (hV : ∃ (C : ∀ n : ℕ, Cone (V.properFaceDiagram n))
        (μ : ∀ n : ℕ, V _⦋n⦌ ⟶ (C n).pt),
      (C 0).pt = Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 X) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (C n))) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : SimplicialObject.ProperFaceCategory n),
        μ n ≫ (C n).π.app (op b) = V.map b.obj.hom.op) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Presieve.singleton (μ n) ∈ Scheme.ProEt.precoverage X (C n).pt))
    (wU : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (U _⦋n⦌))
    (wV : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (V _⦋n⦌))
    (hg : ∀ n : ℕ, g n ≫ (U _⦋n⦌).hom = (V _⦋n⦌).hom ≫ f)
    (hnat : ∀ (m n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (a : m ⟶ n),
      (V.map a).left ≫ g n.unop.len = g m.unop.len ≫ (U.map a).left)
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X Y))
    (hbij : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
      (componentLiftSectionPullback Λ (g n) ((upperStar Λ.X (U _⦋n⦌).hom).obj M))) :
    IsIso ((condensedModuleSections Λ.X Y).rightDerivedFunctor.map
      ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction Λ.X f).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)))
